commits.pr_title: [Structured Output] Keep invalid structured-output requests from stopping the engine
commits.pr_body:
# Keep invalid structured-output requests from stopping the engine

## What this fixes

`-1` values used only to pad speculative-decoding token rows were passed into structured-output
grammars, which treat every entry as a real token id. On an affected backend this mishandled the
padded block once it reached the grammar.

This strips the padding in the scheduler, immediately before tokens are handed to
`grammar.accept_tokens`, so the guard is backend-agnostic and covers any current or future backend
rather than living in one backend.

## Why it matters

Any client allowed to request structured output could reach this path with an ordinary request.
Structured output is a normal API feature; no filesystem or administrator access is required. The
impact is service loss, not code execution or data access.

## Scope reduced during review

Following @arpera's review, this PR was trimmed to a single fix:

- **PTP-VLLM-028** (backend compile failures) was dropped — the scheduler's
  `grammar_compile_error_reqs` path already finishes grammar-compile failures as per-request
  errors, so the change was redundant.
- **PTP-VLLM-043** (Rust empty values) was split into its own PR, #54821, so it can land
  independently.
- **PTP-VLLM-029** (this PR) — the `-1` padding filter was moved out of the Guidance backend into
  the scheduler so it applies to every backend.

## The change

| Site | What now happens |
|---|---|
| PTP-VLLM-029 — speculative padding | `_strip_speculative_padding` removes `-1` sentinels (and everything after the first one) in the scheduler, before tokens reach any backend. |

## How it was tested

`pytest tests/v1/structured_output/test_scheduler_speculative_padding.py` — 4 cases covering
trailing padding, leading padding, no padding, and truncation at the first sentinel.

## Reference

Advisory: GHSA-85xf-c7hm-whqw

Track B: this is a public PR against `vllm-project/vllm@main`.

- @KernelClint (Clinton Thomas) and @dhalf (Lucas Bourtoule)
- Patch the Planet (Trail of Bits + OpenAI collaboration)
- AI assistance was used in preparing this change (model: GPT-5.5-Cyber); every changed line has
  been reviewed and is defended by the human submitter.

All commits include DCO `Signed-off-by` trailers.

commits.pr_title: [Refactor][kv_offload]: rename `block`→`chunk`
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The KV offloading framework has two granularities: **block** (GPU allocator unit, one block-table entry) and **chunk** (offloading transfer unit, one or more blocks grouped via `blocks_per_chunk`).
The code conflated them because `blocks_per_chunk` was historically always 1.

This PR fixes the naming so "block" only refers to GPU blocks, and "chunk" refers to the offloading/tiering unit. No behavioral changes.

Key renames:
- `BlockStatus`→`ChunkSlotStatus`, 
- `_num_blocks`→`_num_chunks`,
- `batch_store_block`→`batch_store_chunks`, 
- `BLOCK_QUERIES`→`CHUNK_QUERIES`,
- `TransferJob.block_ids`→`TransferJob.chunk_slot_ids` (these were CPU slot indices, not GPU block IDs — the rename makes that explicit).

## Breaking changes

Unreleased APIs, no external consumers:
- `TransferJob.block_ids` → `.chunk_slot_ids`
- `BlockStatus` → `ChunkSlotStatus`
- C extension: `batch_store_block`/`batch_load_block` → `batch_store_chunks`/`batch_load_chunks`
- Metrics: `*_block_queries` → `*_chunk_queries`, `*_block_hits` → `*_chunk_hits`

commits.pr_title: [Qwen4Exp] Support UVA PLE-offload and Engram tensor parallelism
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose Add UVA-based PLE offload and Engram tensor parallelism (ETP) for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next. `--engram-config` controls PLE weight storage and embedding sharding: - `cpu_offload=true` stores each local PLE weight shard in pinned CPU memory. The GPU reads the required rows directly through CUDA Unified Virtual Addressing (UVA), using a dedicated CUDA stream. Offload can also be enabled with `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=1` when `cpu_offload` is omitted; an explicit `cpu_offload` value takes precedence. - `cpu_offload=false` keeps PLE weights on the GPU. - `embedding_across_dp=false` uses `ETP=TP`, keeping a separate TP-sharded PLE table in each DP replica. - `embedding_across_dp=true` uses `ETP=TP×DP`, sharding the PLE table across all DP replicas. Offload and cross-DP sharding can be enabled independently. Both options default to false. ## Design The PLE embedding implementation is organized into three abstraction levels: ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph Level1["Level 1 — N-gram embedding semantics"] NGram["Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding
computes request-dependent n-gram IDs
and orchestrates forward/prefetch"] end subgraph Level2["Level 2 — device-specific storage and execution"] Device["Qwen4ExpPLEDeviceEmbedding
GPU-resident weights
resident forward path
prefetch is a no-op"] Pinned["Qwen4ExpPinnedHostEmbedding
pinned CPU weights
UVA lookup on a side stream
prefetch and finalization"] end subgraph Level3["Level 3 — common embedding and weight-format foundation"] Base["Qwen4ExpPLEEmbedding
common backend interface
ETP sharding, DP ID gathering
and local-row selection"] Method["Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod
weight creation, lookup format
and dequantization interface"] BF16["Qwen4ExpPLEUnquantizedEmbeddingMethod
BF16 embedding"] FP8["Qwen4ExpPLEFp8EmbeddingMethod
FP8 embedding and global scale"] end NGram -->|"owns one backend selected at initialization"| Device NGram -->|"owns one backend selected at initialization"| Pinned Device -.->|"inherits"| Base Pinned -.->|"inherits"| Base Base -->|"delegates weight-format behavior"| Method Method --> BF16 Method --> FP8 ``` - `Qwen4ExpNGramEmbedding` contains the model-specific n-gram computation and coordinates `start_prefetch()` and `forward()`. - `Qwen4ExpPLEDeviceEmbedding` and `Qwen4ExpPinnedHostEmbedding` encapsulate device-specific allocation and execution. The pinned-host backend implements the asynchronous UVA path, while the device backend retains the resident lookup path. - `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbedding` provides the shared embedding contract and ETP logic. It delegates weight-format-specific creation and dequantization to `Qwen4ExpPLEEmbeddingMethod`, with separate BF16 and FP8 implementations. ## Not a duplicate Searched the open PRs for [Qwen4Exp PLE offload](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+Qwen4Exp+PLE+offload), and [PLE UVA](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Aopen+PLE+UVA). There are related PRs, but they use materially different designs: - [#53899](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53899) uses a dedicated CPU offload worker and transfers selected rows back to GPU workers. This PR keeps the table in process-local pinned memory and lets the GPU read the required rows directly through UVA, without an offload worker or IPC row transfer. - [#54129](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54129) uses disk-backed mmap storage to reduce host-memory residency. This PR intentionally keeps the complete local shard pinned in RAM for direct UVA access. - [#54431](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54431) optimizes ragged n-gram ID generation for the worker-based offload path. - [#54517](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54517) fuses the PLE compute kernels and is orthogonal to the pinned-table storage, asynchronous UVA lookup, and NP topology introduced here. ## Test Plan ```bash python -m pytest -q tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py python -m pytest -q tests/engine/test_arg_utils.py -k engram python -m pytest -q tests/test_config.py -k engram git diff --check ``` ## End-to-end validation: Run Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with TP4, DP2, and MTP3 for all four `--engram-config` combinations: | `cpu_offload` | `embedding_across_dp` | Expected PLE storage | Expected ETP topology | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | false | false | GPU memory | ETP4, a separate TP-sharded table per DP replica | | false | true | GPU memory | ETP8, one table sharded across both DP replicas | | true | false | Pinned CPU memory | ETP4, a separate TP-sharded table per DP replica | | true | true | Pinned CPU memory | ETP8, one table sharded across both DP replicas | For each combination, verify storage and topology against the table, exercise CUDA Graph capture and replay with uneven DP loads (including an idle replica), and run GSM8K. ## Test Result - Added and updated PLE, Engram configuration, and CLI tests: 50 passed. - Ruff checks on the PLE, Engram configuration, and communicator files: passed. - `git diff --check`: passed. - BF16 TP2/DP1/MTP3 startup and serving with `cpu_offload=true` and `embedding_across_dp=false`: passed. - Both TP ranks reported BF16 PLE weights on CPU with pinned storage enabled. - GSM8K: `0.9727` mean accuracy over 1,319 samples. ## Performance Results Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8`. Prefill uses 8K input at concurrency 2; decode uses 1024 output tokens at concurrency 64 with MTP=3. The workloads use synthetic random-token inputs. The `cpu_offload` and `embedding_across_dp` columns correspond to fields in `--engram-config`. | `cpu_offload` | `embedding_across_dp` | Parallel Configuration | Prefill tok/s | Raw Decode tok/s | Draft Acceptance | Seq-steps/s | Est. commits.pr_title: [Transformers backend] Enable QKV-Fuser for Gemma4
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Enable the Transformers-backend QKV fuser to fire on **Gemma 4** attention. The
fuser merges `q(x), k(x), v(x)` into a single `QKVParallelLinear` GEMM by
rewriting the module's forward *source*, but Gemma 4's attention broke three of
its assumptions:

1. **`v_proj` is referenced beyond its single call** — Gemma 4 guards the call
   with a presence check (`v_proj is not None`). The old rewrite required each
   projection to appear exactly once, so it refused.
2. **q/k/v calls are split across branches** — `q` sits at body level while
   `k`/`v` live inside the `else` of `if self.is_kv_shared_layer:`, so no single
   block contains all three calls.
3. **The forward mutates a container** — `shared_kv_states[...] = ...` item
   assignment ended the fx trace early.

Changes:

- **Fold existence guards to a constant.** The fuser only binds instances where
  the projection exists as a truthy `nn.Linear` (guaranteed by the match, the
  cache key, and `validate`), so a guard testing its presence has a constant
  value. `bypass_existence_guard` folds `is` / `is not None` comparisons, in
  either operand order, to the right bool, and folds a **bare truthiness** test
  (`... if self.v_proj else ...`, `not self.v_proj`, `if self.v_proj:`) to
  `True`. `==` / `!=` are deliberately **not** folded: `is_linear` accepts
  `nn.Linear` subclasses that may override `__eq__` / `__ne__`, so equality is
  not guaranteed to track identity. Any other surviving reference (e.g.
  `isinstance(self.v_proj, ...)`, `self.v_proj.weight`, an `and` / `or` operand
  whose value can escape) is not foldable, so the fuser refuses rather than
  change semantics.
- **Hoist the fused GEMM to the dominating block.** `block_chain` replaces
  `innermost_block`, returning the path of `(block, index)` pairs to each call;
  the fused GEMM is inserted before the earliest call, in the innermost block
  common to all three. Live branches survive the rewrite.
- **Trace past item assignment.** `_MetaProxy.__setitem__` records
  `obj[key] = value` as `operator.setitem` so tracing continues.
- **Lift both safety checks onto `StackedFuser`.** Every stacked fuser deletes
  the projections it merges, so guard folding is not specific to QKV:
  `StackedFuser._unguarded_calls` now resolves each projection's call and folds
  any guard on it, and is used by `QKVFuser`, `MergedColumnParallelFuser`,
  `GLUFuser` and `MLAFuser`. Alongside it, `_check_input_stable` replaces
  `MergedColumnParallelFuser`'s structural whitelist with a dataflow check: the
  merged GEMM is evaluated once at the insertion point, so it must read what the
  last call would have. `aliasing_names` tracks the input's names plus anything
  that may alias them (a view shares storage), `written_names` catches rebinding,
  writes through a name, and calls that write an argument (`inplace=`, `out=`,
  `torch.relu_(x)`), and `_returns_fresh` keeps freshly allocated results and
  dead branches from tainting. Both sides over-approximate, since a false hit
  costs a fusion while a miss returns wrong numbers.

The rewrite is a structural transform only — the fused forward is numerically
equivalent to the original (merged GEMM + split with the same weight mapping).

## Limitations

This fuses the layers that own a full q/k/v triple. Two Gemma 4 layer shapes are
intentionally left:

- **Global `k==v` layers** (`attention_k_eq_v` / `use_alternative_attention`):
  `v_proj` is `None` and value reuses key, so only q and k projections exist —
  no triple to merge. Fusing q+k here needs a separate QK fuser (follow-up PR).
- **KV-shared layers** (the last `num_kv_shared_layers`): only `q_proj` exists;
  k/v are read from `shared_kv_states`, so there is nothing to fuse.

Checkpoints using the defaults (`attention_k_eq_v=False`,
`num_kv_shared_layers=0`) have only standard layers, so all of them fuse.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/transformers/fusers/ -v
```

The whole fusers/ directory, not just test_linear.py: merged_column.py,
glu.py and mla.py all changed.

New/extended coverage in test_linear.py:

- test_fuses_gemma4_qkv_obstacles — guarded v_proj (None, ternary
  truthiness, statement-form if) and branch-split k/v all fuse, with a
  numerics-equivalence check.
- test_qkv_refuses_unsound_rewrites — a rebound input, in-place mutation
  (x.mul_, x[...] = 0), mutation through a view, a functional in-place call
  (F.relu(x, inplace=True)), and a non-guard v_proj reference all fail
  closed.
- test_fuses_real_gemma4_attention — the real Gemma4TextAttention fuses, for
  both the sliding and full-attention layers (which differ in head_dim).
- test_bypass_existence_guard_* — every None-comparison form and operand
  order folds to the correct bool; bare truthiness folds to True; == / !=
  and other non-guard references raise.
- test_merged_column_fuser_folds_existence_guard and
  test_merged_column_fuser_rejects_input_mutation — guard folding and the
  input-stability check are exercised through a non-QKV stacked fuser.

In test_mla.py:

- test_update_forward_rewrites_real_attention — the real
  DeepseekV2Attention source rewrite survives the new check, for both q-LoRA
  configurations.

## Test Result

tests/models/transformers/fusers/            105 passed, 1 skipped
tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_linear.py   58 passed, 1 skipped

End-to-end on the real checkpoint (`google/gemma-4-E2B-it`, CPU):

- Both fusers fire: `q_proj + k_proj + v_proj -> qkv_proj (QKVParallelLinear)`
  and `gate_proj + up_proj -> gate_up_proj (MergedColumnParallelLinear)`.
- Greedy output is **byte-identical** to the unfused native `gemma4.py` path on
  the same prompt, which rules out mis-sharded q/k/v weights rather than only
  proving the rewritten AST is equivalent.
- Chat-templated generation is correct: "What is the capital of France?" answers
  `Paris`.

Run with `limit_mm_per_prompt={'audio': 0}`, needed because
`get_max_audio_tokens` cannot read a max length from `Gemma4AudioConfig`. That
is a pre-existing gap in the Transformers-backend multimodal path, unrelated to
this PR, and I will file it separately.

This is a single greedy prompt on CPU, not an eval sweep. Happy to run lm_eval
on a GPU box if a reviewer wants an accuracy number.

cc @hmellor

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix unreachable None guard in Molmo2 get_candidate_target_fps
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

In `Molmo2VideoBackend.get_candidate_target_fps`, the `sampling_fps is None` guard is placed **after** `sampling_fps = int(sampling_fps)`:

```python
video_fps = int(video_fps)
sampling_fps = int(sampling_fps)   # int(None) -> TypeError HERE
max_fps = int(max_fps)

if sampling_fps is None:           # dead code: never reached when None
    raise ValueError("sampling_fps must be provided")
```

When `sampling_fps is None`, `int(None)` raises an opaque `TypeError: int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a real number, not 'NoneType'` before the guard runs — so the intended clear `ValueError("sampling_fps must be provided")` is dead code.

`sampling_fps` flows from `target.fps` at the `frame_sample_mode == "fps"` call site, which can be `None`, so this path is reachable.

## Fix

Move the `None` guard before the `int()` coercions.

## Test Plan

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Skip undefined token ids in decode and anchor them zero-width
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`HuggingFaceTokenizer::decode` has three backends. The `tokenizers` backend and the generic `fastokens` backend both skip an id the vocabulary does not define: `tokenizers 0.22` decodes through `filter_map`, and `fastokens 0.2.1` does so explicitly ("Match HuggingFace behavior: silently skip unknown IDs (e.g. models like Qwen3-0.6B-FP8 emit IDs in the gap between tokenizer.json's vocab and the embedding matrix). Erroring here would kill streaming generation on a single bad token."). The wrapper's own byte-level fast path, taken for every tokenizer whose decoder is a single `ByteLevel` step (GPT-2-style BPE, so the Qwen families), instead fails the whole decode with `decoding failed: unknown token ID: <id>`. Through the incremental detokenizer that turns one sampled id from the padded region of the lm_head into a failed stream and an aborted request; a Qwen3.5-9B run hit it once in 800 random-prompt requests (config `vocab_size` 248320, tokenizer ids up to 248069), and Qwen3-4B carries 267 such ids. Padded ids are legal argmax outputs; the two other backends and HF's Python tokenizer already treat them as empty.

This PR makes the byte-level fast path skip undefined ids the way the backend it accelerates does, so all three arms agree, and replaces the test that pinned the error with one that pins the agreement.

The incremental decoder had the same gap one layer up. A generated id the vocabulary does not define was recorded as pending, and when the next defined token produced text every pending token was anchored `Visible` at that text's start, so the undefined id was reported as a producer of text it never contributed. `DecodeStream` now anchors such an id `ZeroWidth` where it fell; the vocabulary lookup runs only for a token that produced no new text. The seeding path's doc comment loses its sentence about generated ids taking a strict path, which no longer holds for the HF backends. The `tokenizers` and generic `fastokens` backends, which already skipped undefined ids, misattributed them the same way before this PR. Not a duplicate: no open PR or issue touches this decode path or mentions undefined ids in the Rust tokenizer (searched `unknown token ID` and `undefined token` across issues and PRs); the erroring test came in unchanged with the code move in #43283 and no PR since has revisited it, while `fastokens` fixed the same case on its side.

No model evaluation is needed: no sampling changes; a request that decoded before decodes to the same text, and a request that failed now decodes with the undefined id contributing nothing, which is the behaviour of the other two backends. AI assistance was used for this change; the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.


## Test Plan

```
cd rust
cargo nextest run -p vllm-tokenizer
cargo clippy -p vllm-tokenizer --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo nextest run -p vllm-text
```

New tests: `fast_byte_level_skips_undefined_ids` — on the crate's tiny byte-level BPE fixture, a sequence with an undefined id in the middle decodes to the same text as the sequence without it; it replaces `fast_byte_level_errors_on_unknown_id`, which pinned the divergence. `decode_stream_anchors_undefined_ids_zero_width` — a `create_decode_stream` over the wrapper built on the same fixture (byte-level backend asserted) pushes `[999, 1, 999, 2]` and, after `flush`, the text is `He` with attributions `999 ZeroWidth@0, 1 Visible@0, 999 ZeroWidth@1, 2 Visible@1`. Two test mocks whose `id_to_token` was `unreachable!()` now return a token string, since the stream consults it for a token that produced no text.

Reproduction outside the test suite (a throwaway example, not part of this PR): load Qwen3-4B's `tokenizer.json` through `HuggingFaceTokenizer::new` (it takes the byte-level fast path; `vocab_size()` reports 151,669 against the model's 151,936-wide lm_head) and decode `[151700]` and `[9707, 151700, 1879]` (`Hello world` with an undefined id inserted).

## Test Result

Without the decode fix the first test fails on the base commit:

```
thread 'hf::tests::fast_byte_level_skips_undefined_ids' panicked at src/tokenizer/src/hf.rs:729:69:
with the id: TokenizerError("decoding failed: unknown token ID: 999")
```

With the decode fix alone the stream test fails, which is the misattribution:

```
thread 'hf::tests::decode_stream_anchors_undefined_ids_zero_width' panicked at src/tokenizer/src/hf.rs:759:9:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: [(999, Visible { byte_offset: 0 }), (1, Visible { byte_offset: 0 }), (999, Visible { byte_offset: 1 }), (2, Visible { byte_offset: 1 })]
 right: [(999, ZeroWidth { byte_offset: 0 }), (1, Visible { byte_offset: 0 }), (999, ZeroWidth { byte_offset: 1 }), (2, Visible { byte_offset: 1 })]
```

With both: `cargo nextest run -p vllm-tokenizer` 89 tests run, 89 passed; `cargo clippy -p vllm-tokenizer --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo nextest run -p vllm-text` 90 passed, 1 skipped, identical to the base.

The reproduction on the real tokenizer, base then this branch:

```
decode([151700])             = Err(tokenizer error: decoding failed: unknown token ID: 151700)
decode([9707, 151700, 1879]) = Err(tokenizer error: decoding failed: unknown token ID: 151700)

decode([151700])             = Ok("")
decode([9707, 151700, 1879]) = Ok("Hello world")
```

commits.pr_title: [Rust Frontend] Make --max-model-len optional for the render server
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The Rust render server required `--max-model-len` as a mandatory CLI flag, even though it is an engine-free tokenizer server that does not run a model. The value is only used for prompt-length validation and `max_tokens` capping in the request lowering path.

This PR makes `--max-model-len` optional:
- When provided, the render server validates prompt length against it (existing behavior as on main branch)
- When omitted, `build_state` falls back to `u32::MAX`, which makes the comparison a no-op and leaves the length check to the vLLM engine. The engine still enforces the real limit.This avoids replicating the complex HF config derivation logic (RoPE scaling, field precedence, tokenizer clamping) in the Rust renderer, which would be error-prone and drift from the Python implementation over time.
-`u32::MAX` is an internal value and must not escape to clients. `/v1/models` previously read the value back out of `TextRequestProcessor`, where the `Option` has already been collapsed, so omitting the flag made the model card advertise a `4294967295`-token context window instead of reporting that no limit is configured. `RenderState` now keeps the configured `Option<u32>` alongside the processor, so the card emits `null`

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Exclude DP token padding from draft attention metadata
commits.pr_body:
DeepSeek-V3.2 DP8 + EP + MTP crashes when DP ranks have unequal request counts. A rank with 12 requests receives model inputs padded to 13 tokens; the sparse indexer then fails with `shape '[12, -1, 64, 128]' is invalid for input of size 106496`. Validation:
- The exact [H200 large-model job in build 87389](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87389#01a0712c-2e18-480d-bda7-dfac8725ed44) passed all **6 evaluations** on implementation commit `39ba6cbae8e1`. DeepSeek-V3.2-DP scored **0.9568**, above its **0.8700** lower bound.

Those imports are now removed. `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/v1/spec_decode/test_eagle_draft_attn_metadata.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py` and `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh targeted H200 validation for current head `c34119ecbe4d` is [build 87771](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/87771). Its result is pending; the older passing run above is not represented as current-head validation.

Duplicate checks found no competing PR for the one-query-per-request draft-decode metadata mismatch. Related #53660, #54102, and #53577 address draft prefill, verifier residual padding, and DSpark PP respectively. This PR updates the existing fix rather than introducing a second implementation.

## Purpose

On non-Harmony models, `/v1/responses` returns HTTP 500 for any input item that pydantic accepts through the openai SDK union but that vLLM does not handle. Examples are `item_reference`, `computer_call_output`, and `mcp_call`.

It is the same error class the function already raises for encrypted reasoning content, and the same approach #55701 applied to the Harmony path. Plain dicts that already carry a `role` still pass through unchanged, so user, system, and developer messages are unaffected. The assistant dict with `content=[]` is owned by #48237 and #49130 and is not touched here.

Not a duplicate. Open Responses PRs #55662, #35508, #50975, #54786, #54297 each handle one specific item type and leave the fall-through in place. Searches for `item_reference 500`, `responses KeyError role`, and `unsupported input item type` return nothing.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Fix Mooncake heterogeneous TP with replicated GQA heads
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix Mooncake heterogeneous-TP KV transfer when a standard GQA layout crosses the KV-head replication boundary. This includes both:

- Prefill TP > `num_kv_heads` >= Decode TP, where producer ranks contain replicated head slices that must be gathered into the Decode KV block;
- Prefill TP <= `num_kv_heads` < Decode TP, where unique Prefill head slices must be fanned out to replicated Decode ranks.

The heterogeneous-TP planner previously treated `producer_cache_replicated=True` as if every producer rank held a full copy of the KV block. That is not true when `num_kv_heads < producer_tp_size`: each unique KV head is replicated, but a rank still owns only one head-sized slice. The reverse direction also used TP-ratio offsets after the consumer crossed into head replication, which selected the wrong source slice and failed the pre-transfer region-length validation.

For example, with four KV heads, TP8 Prefill, and TP1 Decode:

- each Prefill rank has one 65,536-byte head slice, replicated twice;
- Decode expects a 262,144-byte block containing all four heads;
- the old planner selects only rank 0 and writes offset 0;
- the remaining 196,608 bytes are not transferred, but Decode still marks the request KV-ready because Mooncake reports the selected copy as successful.

We originally observed this with a custom-quantized MiniMax M3 deployment, but reproduced it on official vLLM v0.27.1 with the upstream-supported Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 model. The issue is therefore in the generic Mooncake
heterogeneous-TP planner, not the custom model or quantization.

This change:

- detects when producer and consumer cache replication states differ;
- maps each paired producer/consumer rank through its global KV-head index;
- selects one canonical producer for each replicated producer head;
- applies the corresponding source or destination head offset in both transfer directions;
- avoids applying pure TP-ratio region-length validation when either side is replicated;
- leaves MLA and TP relationships with matching replication states on the
  existing planner path.

### Duplicate-work check

I searched open PRs for `Mooncake heterogeneous TP GQA`, `Mooncake replicated KV heads`, and `Mooncake tensor parallel`. No other PR addresses this defect. The closest open work covers PP/PCP metadata (#46004 and #49109) or RDMA device discovery (#44919), not replicated GQA-head transfer across heterogeneous TP.

#53078 fixes heterogeneous-TP state transfer for hybrid Mamba/GDN models, while this PR fixes replicated-GQA head mapping across heterogeneous TP configurations. If #53078 lands first, I would consider stacking/rebasing this PR on top of it and reconciling the two paths there.

## Test Plan

Focused unit tests:

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONPATH=. .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_connector/unit \
  -k 'sender_plan or region_length_validation'
```

Lint and static checks:

```bash
pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_connector.py
```

End-to-end fan-in reproduction:

- official vLLM v0.27.1 code and image;
- Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 with four KV heads;
- TP8 Prefill to DP8/TP1 Decode through Mooncake RDMA;
- deterministic one-token request through the PD router.

## Test Result

- Focused sender-plan and region-validation tests: `41 passed, 30 deselected`.
- All selected pre-commit hooks passed, including ruff, format, mypy, SPDX, forbidden-import, and lazy-import checks.
- A local reference-mapping check validated all 125 combinations where Prefill TP, Decode TP, and KV-head count were selected from `{1, 2, 4, 8, 16}` under the existing divisibility constraints.

### Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 reproduction

Without the fix, Decode receives only one of the four unique KV-head slices. The other three destination regions remain unwritten, but Decode treats the block as complete and uses it for attention. The request does not fail at the
API or transport layer, so the resulting token corruption is silent.

The pre-fix transfer log for the first attention layer shows that rank 0 is the only sender:

```text
rank=0 should_transfer=true  dst_offset=0      transfer_len=65536
rank=2 should_transfer=false dst_offset=0      transfer_len=65536
rank=4 should_transfer=false dst_offset=0      transfer_len=65536
rank=6 should_transfer=false dst_offset=0      transfer_len=65536
```

Decode then marks the request ready without reporting an error:

```text
pull_tasks_count=0 response_status=0
KV Transfer metrics: Num successful transfers=1, Num failed transfers=0, Num failed recvs=0
```

This means only 65,536 of the expected 262,144 bytes are written, for 25% destination coverage. In the deterministic one-token smoke test, the API still returned HTTP 200, but Qwen3 produced a newline as its first token:

```json
{"content":"\n","finish_reason":"length"}
```

After the fix, one canonical replica for each unique KV head contributes its slice:

```text
rank=0 should_transfer=true dst_offset=0      transfer_len=65536
rank=2 should_transfer=true dst_offset=65536  transfer_len=65536
rank=4 should_transfer=true dst_offset=131072 transfer_len=65536
rank=6 should_transfer=true dst_offset=196608 transfer_len=65536
```

The four writes cover the full 262,144-byte destination block. Mooncake reports four successful transfers with no failures:

```text
KV Transfer metrics: Num successful transfers=4, Num failed transfers=0, Num failed recvs=0
```

The same deterministic request returned HTTP 200 and produced Qwen3's
`<think>` token:

```json
{"content":"<think>","finish_reason":"length"}
```

The one-token result is a smoke test rather than an accuracy benchmark. Its purpose is to show that the incomplete KV block affected Qwen3 decoding even though the request appeared successful. The reverse fan-out direction is
covered by the focused unit tests; it has not been rerun in a multi-node Mooncake deployment.

The equivalent mapping fix was also evaluated in the original custom-quantized MiniMax M3 deployment:

- GSM8K 0-shot: 1274 / 1319 (96.59%).
- AIME25 repeat-4: 97 / 120 (80.83%).
- GPQA Diamond: 177 / 198 (89.39%).

Before the mapping fix, a focused GSM8K run produced 0 / 8 correct responses and all eight generations hit the 65,536-token limit. After the fix, the systematic corruption and truncation behavior disappeared. The Qwen3
reproduction above independently verifies that the underlying bug and fix are not MiniMax-specific.

commits.pr_title: [CI/Build][Hardware][NVIDIA] Add public CUDA 13.4 Rubin build path
commits.pr_body:
NVIDIA now publishes a CUDA 13.4 developer-preview apt repo publicly (`packages.nvidia.com`), and `pytorch/manylinux2_28-builder` already has a `cuda13.4`-tagged image on Docker Hub. This adds an `INSTALL_RUBIN_PRERELEASE` (#53443) path that uses both, so a fully public build is possible.

## What's in this PR

- `BUILD_BASE_IMAGE`: `pytorch/manylinux2_28-builder:cuda13.4` (and the aarch64 equivalent) - already bundles a full CUDA 13.4 toolkit, no changes needed for the wheel-build stage.
- `FINAL_BASE_IMAGE`: the public, multi-arch `nvcr.io/nvidia/cuda-dl-base:26.08-cuda13.4-devel-ubuntu24.04` image. It already bundles nvcc/nvrtc-dev, `PATH`/`CUDA_HOME`, NCCL 2.30.7, and GDRCopy 2.5.1, so none of the plain-`ubuntu:24.04` workarounds below are needed against it. New `CUDA_PREVIEW_APT_REPO`/`_SUITE` args (still set, harmless no-op against this image) register NVIDIA's public developer-preview apt repo (`packages.nvidia.com/noble`, `prerelease/cuda/13.4.0`) for anyone who still wants a plain `ubuntu:24.04` final image instead - the same mechanism sglang uses for their own CUDA 13.4 container (sgl-project/sglang#36233).
- `requirements/rubin-prerelease.txt`: a real, public pin set (torch/torchvision/torchaudio cu134 nightlies, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.8.0.dev0`, `flashinfer-python`) so `INSTALL_RUBIN_PRERELEASE=true` works out of the box without every caller needing to hand-write this file. Happy to instead move this to caller-supplied/untracked if maintainers prefer that over a committed file - flagging as an open question.
- Two internal-image assumptions in the existing `INSTALL_RUBIN_PRERELEASE` code needed adjusting for this path: GDRCopy/NCCL checks are now reality-based (check `ldconfig`/`find` for the actual library, tolerate not finding it) instead of inferred from whether `CUDA_PREVIEW_APT_REPO` is set - this makes both the internal-image and public-image (including `cuda-dl-base`) paths work correctly. `PATH`/`CUDA_HOME`/`LD_LIBRARY_PATH` are set explicitly in the runtime stage as a fallback for plain-`ubuntu:24.04` builds that don't bake these in.
- `cuda-nvrtc-dev-${CUDA_VERSION_DASH}` added to the CUDA dev tools install: FlashInfer's runtime-JIT-compiled kernels `#include <nvrtc.h>`, which only the `-dev` package ships; the existing list only installed the runtime-only `cuda-nvrtc` package.

## Not duplicating existing work

Not duplicating #53443 or the earlier #52379 (which #53443 superseded as the community-accepted mechanism): #53443's own author described its design as accepting "caller-supplied CUDA 13.4 build/runtime images" (see the #49735 comment thread). This PR fills that gap with an actual public recipe, since the current docs only describe an NVIDIA-internal one.

## Test plan

Built and live-tested end-to-end on both architectures.

- amd64 (x86 Rubin node): CI build green (`py3-base`/`py3-devel`), `vllm serve` starts and serves real, correct completions.
- arm64 (aarch64 Rubin node): same, plus full CI manifest/devel pipeline green.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][EC Connector] Fix ECExampleConnector load device under TP>1
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

`ECExampleConnector.start_load_caches` passed the bare device string `"cuda"`
to `safetensors.torch.load_file`. Safetensors resolves that to `cuda:0`, even
when a tensor-parallel worker is running on another selected device.

Under `tensor_parallel_size > 1`, a non-rank-0 worker could therefore load the
encoder cache on `cuda:0` and later fail when combining it with tensors on its
local device. This was reproduced on vLLM v0.17.0 with Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct,
TP=4, and 4 x L4 GPUs.

## Fix

Pin CUDA-like loads to the device selected by vLLM's platform abstraction:

```python
device = current_platform.device_type
if current_platform.is_cuda_alike():
    device = f"{device}:{current_platform.current_device()}"
```

The platform abstraction keeps this compatible with CUDA-like backends, while
non-CUDA platforms continue to receive their unchanged `device_type`.

Two regression tests cover both paths:

- CUDA-like platforms load onto the selected device (for example, `cuda:2`).
- Non-CUDA platforms keep the bare platform device type.

## Validation

- [x] GitHub `pre-commit` workflow passes on the amended commit.
- [x] `check-torch-cuda-call`, Ruff check/format, and mypy 3.12 pass locally on
      the changed files.
- [x] The repository's manual-stage hook suite passes locally, excluding the
      Docker graph hook and Linux-only non-root entrypoint check on macOS.
- [ ] Full CI: [Buildkite #82780](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/82780)
      (running).

The focused pytest file could not be rerun in the current macOS ARM environment
because vLLM does not publish a compatible precompiled wheel for that platform;
the regression tests are included in the requested Linux/GPU CI run.

commits.pr_title: [Refactor][EC Connector] Add backend extension points to ECCPUWorker
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Purpose

`ECCPUWorker` provides the shared execution model for CPU-backed encoder-cache offloading. It owns the shared mmap layout, descriptor management, transfer batching, Event-based completion tracking, save reconstruction, load reconstruction, and worker metadata reporting.

Device backends use the same lifecycle while supplying their platform-specific Host-memory registration and transfer operations.

This implementation supports the Ascend backend introduced by:

https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/pull/13894

## Backend Extension Points

`ECCPUWorker` exposes three backend extension points.

### `_pin_shared_region`

Prepares the shared mmap region for device transfers.

The base implementation uses vLLM's standard Host-memory pinning path. `AscendECCPUWorker` uses this point to register the mmap as pinned Host memory through CANN.

### `_submit_transfer`

Submits a batch of transfer descriptors for H2D or D2H execution.

The base implementation dispatches through `swap_blocks_batch`. `AscendECCPUWorker` dispatches through the corresponding CANN batched-copy operation.

`ECCPUTransferDirection` identifies the H2D or D2H direction passed to the backend implementation.

### `_shutdown_transfer_backend`

Performs backend-specific shutdown after the common worker lifecycle has waited for tracked in-flight transfer Events.

Device backends use this point for platform synchronization, transfer-resource release, and pinned Host-memory unregistration. The common shutdown path then releases worker state and cleans up the shared region.

With these extension points, device workers inherit the upstream `save_caches`, `flush_saves`, `start_load_caches`, completion reporting, buffer recycling, and shutdown lifecycle.

## Model Runner Support

`ECCPUConnector` supports Model Runner V2 only.

## Test Plan

### CPU and mock regression

```bash

  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/test_worker_ec_connector.py \

  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/cpu/test_connector.py \
  tests/v1/ec_connector/unit/cpu/test_ec_shared_region.py
```

This coverage includes connector construction and role handling, the Model Runner V2 requirement, scheduler behavior, metadata handling, and shared-region lifecycle.

### NVIDIA CUDA worker validation

```bash

```

The worker coverage verifies that both save and load paths delegate transfer submission through `_submit_transfer()` with the correct direction, and that common shutdown invokes `_shutdown_transfer_backend()` before shared-region cleanup.

commits.pr_title: [Core][KV Connector] Resolve connector block tables for every scheduled request
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix an EngineCore crash in `MooncakeStoreConnector` saves:

```
AssertionError: Missing current block table for store request <req_id>
```

Before this fix, `SchedulerOutput.kv_connector_block_state.block_ids` (introduced by #51358) is only populated for (a) newly scheduled requests, (b) cached requests whose `new_block_ids` is truthy, and (c) requests with a Mamba boundary-state hand-off. `MooncakeStoreScheduler._apply_current_save_block_ids` asserts that every save-eligible request has an entry.

But a store save fires on the step that *fills* a block, and the next block is allocated one step *later*. The store scheduler already documents this ("A block is usually allocated before the step that fills it, so reaching a save boundary does not imply that this step has new block ids"), yet the snapshot rule keys on the allocation. With `block_size=16` and `save_decode_cache=true` (#52466):

| step | computed → after | new block? | in snapshot? | save fires? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| N | 47 → 48 | no (token 47 fits block 2) | no | yes (block 2 is full) → **assert** |
| N+1 | 48 → 49 | yes (block 3) | yes | no |

So every decode-phase save misses the snapshot, as does any prefill continuation chunk that lands inside an already-allocated block. Hybrid models with large manager blocks make it near-certain: Kimi-K3 at TP1 has 5760-token blocks and a 128-token store job block, so ~44 of 45 saves miss. Observed on a Kimi-K3 P/D deployment with `save_decode_cache=true` on the decoder: first assert within a minute of traffic, DP engines died one by one, all in-flight requests failed.

### Chunked prefill example

Chunked prefill can hit the same bug without any KV load failure. Consider a producer-side full-attention request with a 96-token prompt, `block_size=16`, and 8 tokens scheduled per step. `save_decode_cache=false` does not prevent this: both steps below are still prefill. Token counts are the number of tokens computed, and block indices are zero-based.

| step | computed → after | new block? | in the old snapshot? | save fires? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| N | 0 → 8 | yes (block 0, with capacity for tokens 0–15) | yes (new request) | no (block 0 is not full yet) |
| N+1 | 8 → 16 | no (the remaining tokens fit in block 0) | no | yes (block 0 is full) → **assert** |

The request is scheduled in both steps, and its current block table still exists in `KVCacheManager`. In the second step, the request is omitted from the old snapshot solely because `new_block_ids` is empty. This PR includes the request whenever it is scheduled, so the save at 8 → 16 can resolve its current table and proceed normally. The same mismatch between allocation and save timing can also occur during prefill recomputation after a failed KV load.

### Fix

Make every request scheduled this step addressable, plus the boundary hand-offs as before. `KVConnectorBlockState` holds the eligible request IDs and a `resolve_block_ids` callback bound to `KVCacheManager.get_block_ids`. Its `get_block_ids(req_id)` method returns `None` for requests outside that set and resolves an eligible request's current table only when the connector asks for it. This avoids eagerly copying tables that the connector never reads, without a separate `Mapping` wrapper.

`MooncakeStoreScheduler` calls `block_state.get_block_ids(req_meta.req_id)` and retains its missing-table assertion. Mamba boundary-state hand-offs are unchanged. The block-state object remains scheduler-local and is cleared before dispatch to workers.

The `DummyKVConnector` test fixture materializes the resolved tables into a plain dict for worker metadata. Its plugin registration is idempotent so multiple tests can use it. The override test also exercises the actual `MessageQueue.enqueue()` serialization path, ensuring the output can be serialized without retaining the scheduler's resolver.

### Why the existing tests did not catch this

The Mooncake store scheduler tests construct scheduler outputs by hand, supplying current block tables even when `new_block_ids=[()]`. Before this fix, the real scheduler omitted those tables on the fill step. The regression drives a real `Scheduler` through that step and checks that the connector can still resolve the request's table. A separate test checks that lookup is lazy, rejects requests outside the offered set without invoking the resolver, and reads the current table on each access.

### Related work (not duplicates)

- #53067 proposes a broader `KVConnectorSchedulerContext` for lazy block access and would supersede this; this PR fixes the crash without introducing the broader connector context API.
- #54643 fixes a second, independent way a save could target a request that is not scheduled (a MultiConnector-rejected `LoadSpec`). Both are needed on a `MultiConnector(NixlConnector, MooncakeStoreConnector)` decoder.
- #54307 (heterogeneous-TP hybrid Store sharing) inherits this bug from `main`; the fix was first validated on top of it.

## Test Plan

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 VLLM_NO_USAGE_STATS=1 \
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_scheduler_kv_connector_override.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py -q

files=(
  vllm/v1/core/sched/output.py
  vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py
  vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/store/scheduler.py
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_scheduler_kv_connector_override.py
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_scheduler.py
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_scheduler.py
)
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files "${files[@]}"
for target_version in 3.11 3.12 3.13; do
  .venv/bin/pre-commit run "mypy-${target_version}" \
    --hook-stage manual --files "${files[@]}"
done
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --all-files --hook-stage manual
```

## Test Result

- Scheduler and connector suites above: **457 passed**. The three override tests were rerun after switching the serialization regression to `MessageQueue`: **3 passed**.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks on the six changed files: **passed**, including mypy for Python 3.10. The manual mypy hooks for Python 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13 also **passed**.
- The previous CI mypy failure was reproduced before the follow-up: the scheduler regression indexed a `tuple[list[int], ...] | None` returned by `.get()`. An explicit `assert block_ids is not None` fixes the narrowing error.
- Full-repository mypy for Python 3.12 reports six missing-attribute errors in two unchanged files: `vllm/models/deepseek_v4/xpu/model.py` (five XPU operator attributes) and `vllm/models/dots3_note/nvidia/vision.py` (`per_block_cast_to_fp8`). The changed files pass their CI checks as noted above.

Previously reported end-to-end result, before this review follow-up: on a Kimi-K3 heterogeneous-TP P/D deployment (TP8 prefill, TP1 decode with `save_decode_cache=true`) on top of #54307, the assert went from ~20 per run to 1 with this change; the remaining one is the #54643 case.

No new model accuracy or end-to-end evaluation was run for this follow-up. The change concerns scheduler block-table lookup and metadata construction; it does not change model computation.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Add NVFP4 support to the torch linear backend
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Extend the existing `torch` linear backend to ModelOpt W4A4 NVFP4 models on
SM10x (Blackwell).

The adapter reuses vLLM's NVFP4 quantization and layout utilities, calls native
`torch._scaled_mm`, applies the ModelOpt global dequantization scale and bias,
and lets `torch.compile`/TorchInductor select an enabled scaled-GEMM backend.
Existing optimized `auto` candidates retain priority; Torch is placed
immediately before emulation and can be selected explicitly with
`--linear-backend torch`.

This does not add or change a custom operator, schema, meta function, or C++
signature, so the custom-op `torch.library.opcheck()` requirements do not
apply.

## Relationship to #36721

This PR references and overlaps #36721, which first proposed an NVFP4
`torch._scaled_mm` backend. It is submitted as a successor/alternative
for review because #36721 is currently several months behind `main`, marked
`needs-rebase`, and its current diff includes unrelated dependency-file changes
from old merges.

The concrete delta here is:

- a clean three-file change on current `main`;
- integration with the shared `--linear-backend torch` registry rather than
  the former NVFP4-specific environment-variable path;
- current weight/activation padding and swizzled-scale layout handling;
- coverage through the existing eager/compiled NVFP4 model test matrix; and
- paired B200 measurements against current FlashInfer CuTeDSL, including its
  normal heuristic and explicitly autotuned tactics.

If maintainers prefer updating #36721 in place, this branch and its results can
be folded into that PR rather than merged independently.

## PyTorch dependency

The vLLM adapter uses native `torch._scaled_mm` and has no dependency on a
vLLM-specific custom operator. The NVGEMM performance configuration measured
below depends on a separate, not-yet-upstream TorchInductor/CuTeDSL stack. The
adapter remains useful with any scaled-GEMM implementation selected by the
installed PyTorch build.

## Test plan and results

- Rebasing onto current `main` produced no conflicts.
- `pre-commit run --files ...`: passed all applicable hooks, including Ruff,
  formatting, mypy, SPDX, configuration, and import checks.
- A supplemental kernel-level smoke sweep compared Torch and vLLM CUTLASS
  directly on the same randomly generated BF16 inputs while varying M over
  `{1, 10, 32, 128, 150}`, covering single-token decode, batched decode, and
  padded/non-padded row counts. Every case passed
  `torch.allclose(atol=0.1, rtol=0.1)`. These tolerances match vLLM's existing
  NVFP4 kernel correctness test in
  `tests/kernels/quantization/test_flashinfer_nvfp4_scaled_mm.py`; the observed
  maximum absolute difference of 0.5 occurred within the combined
  `atol + rtol * abs(reference)` bound. This is supplemental to the exact
  200-example checkpoint-level comparison below.
- With the final native output-scale path and candidate policy, all four Qwen
  projection shapes at M in `{8, 32, 128}` were bit-exact between
  TorchInductor NVGEMM, FlashInfer CuTeDSL, and vLLM CUTLASS: zero differing
  BF16 elements across all 12 cases.
- Actual-checkpoint validation passed with the official
  `nvidia/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-NVFP4` revision
  `bdb54e24298451af785c0ac63c1b485e9b7400a2`. On 200 GSM8K questions
  (five-shot, greedy, 256-token limit), Torch/NVGEMM and vLLM CUTLASS produced
  identical token IDs and text on all 200 examples. Both scored 68.5%
  (137/200), with the same single max-token-limit invalid response. This used
  vLLM's standard prompt builder and scorer from
  `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`.

## End-to-end performance

Environment: GB200 GPU 0, FlashInfer 0.6.17 (`a0a6b019`), 32 input tokens,
128 output tokens, 10 warmups, 30 timed iterations, dummy weights, `-O2`, a
static compile/CUDA-graph size equal to batch size, and detokenization disabled.
These are full prefill-plus-decode latency results from unmodified
`vllm bench latency`; local scripts only orchestrated runs and parsed its JSON.

Torch used NVGEMM with its final scoped candidate policy. FlashInfer's
heuristic column used its normal analytical selection; the tuned column used
vLLM's standard `--enable-flashinfer-autotune` warmup with `mm_fp4` tuning
enabled. Because clocks could not be locked, the table reports paired medians
and uses conservative Torch measurements.

- Dummy weights validate shapes, dispatch, and performance, not model quality.

- The local installed FlashInfer attention stack produced incoherent output

commits.pr_title: [Core] Enhance cpu<->gpu sync checking to include paged async copies
commits.pr_body:
The CPU<->GPU sync checking added in https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/44800 / https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43107 makes use of pytorch's `torch.cuda.set_sync_debug_mode` function.

However this does not catch stalls due to "non-blocking" tensor copies to or from non-pinned host memory, where an implicit copy is made to a staging buffer. This also includes copies from pinned tensors which have non-dense layouts.

This PR extends the sync checking mode by monkeypatching the relevant pytorch methods to check for this.

commits.pr_title: [Kernel] Enable optimized FlashInfer add-RMSNorm NVFP4 fusion
commits.pr_body:
This PR follows up on #36413, which explored the same fusion. Since then, the FlashInfer fused add-RMSNorm + NVFP4 kernel received performance improvements in [flashinfer#4494](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/4494). With these improvements, the kernel brings up positive performance influence on some workloads.

  For `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, the existing path still uses two separate kernels:

  1. An Inductor-generated Triton kernel performs the residual update and RMSNorm.
  2. `cvt_fp16_to_fp4` CUDA kernel computes block scales and converts the intermediate output to FP4.

The FP4 conversion is an opaque custom operator, so Inductor cannot incorporate it into the preceding Triton kernel.
This PR replaces the two-kernel sequence with a single FlashInfer kernel.

In our Qwen3-30B profile, the fusion replaces 47 `add-RMSNorm` kernels and eliminates the corresponding 47 `cvt_fp16_to_fp4` launches per forward pass.

The fusion is disabled by default.

## Performance

The reported numbers are the wall-clock latency of one synchronous local `LLM.generate()` call for a single pre-tokenized prompt. The tested model is `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`, TP1, output length 1. All measured shapes were covered by piecewise CUDA Graph.

Each result is the mean of four independent engine launches using a counterbalanced execution order. Each launch used 200 warm-up iterations followed by 200 measured iterations per shape. All measured shapes were covered by piecewise CUDA Graph.

| GPU | Batch × input length | Existing (mean request latency) | Fused (mean request latency) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| GB200 | 1 × 2048 | 16.467 ms | 16.342 ms | +0.76% |
| GB200 | 1 × 4096 | 26.546 ms | 26.277 ms | +1.02% |
| GB200 | 1 × 8192 | 52.301 ms | 51.811 ms | +0.95% |
| GB300 | 1 × 2048 | 15.741 ms | 15.618 ms | +0.79% |
| GB300 | 1 × 4096 | 24.677 ms | 24.409 ms | +1.10% |
| GB300 | 1 × 8192 | 46.710 ms | 46.214 ms | +1.07% |

## Usage

```json
  {
      "pass_config": {
          "fuse_norm_quant": True,
          "fuse_add_rms_norm_nvfp4": True,
      },
      "max_cudagraph_capture_size": 8192,
      "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1, 2048, 4096, 8192],
  }

```

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Honour the draft's moe_backend on Model Runner V2
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The draft model is loaded with the target's `VllmConfig`, so `--speculative-config '{"moe_backend": ...}'` is ignored on Model Runner V2. When the target is quantized and the draft is not, which is the normal shape of an MTP head, a quantized-only backend rejects the draft and the engine fails to start:

```
ValueError: moe_backend='flashinfer_b12x' is not supported for unquantized MoE.
Expected one of ['triton', 'batched_triton', 'flashinfer_trtllm', 'flashinfer_cutlass', 'aiter'].
```

V1 applies this override in `LLMBaseProposer._create_draft_vllm_config`. V2 never grew the equivalent: `load_eagle_model` overrides `kv_cache_dtype` only, and `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/` contains no reference to `moe_backend` at all. The same command line therefore serves under V1 and fails under V2, which became user-visible when MRV2 was made the default in #53183.

## Fix

Apply the override alongside the existing `kv_cache_dtype` one in `load_eagle_model`. It is scoped to the draft; the target's config is left untouched. MTP reaches this path via `mtp/speculator.py`.

## Validation

Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 with MTP-3 on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q, `--moe-backend flashinfer_b12x` with the draft on `flashinfer_cutlass`. Three arms on one node with identical flags, vLLM `v0.28.1rc1.dev199+g7c5dc571c`:

| arm | runner | fix | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| control | V2 | no | fails with the `ValueError` above |
| treatment | V2 | yes | serves, `Application startup complete` |
| regression | V1 | yes | serves, no V1 change |

```
pytest tests/v1/spec_decode/test_draft_moe_backend_override.py -v   # 3 passed
ruff check <changed files>                                          # All checks passed
```

The tests patch `get_model` to capture the config the draft would be built with, and assert that the override reaches the draft's kernel config, that its absence still inherits the target, and that the target's own config is not mutated. Reverting the fix fails them with the bug's signature:

```
assert used.kernel_config.moe_backend == "flashinfer_cutlass"
AssertionError: assert 'flashinfer_b12x' == 'flashinfer_cutlass'
```

## Why this is not a duplicate

I ran the checks in AGENTS.md. Nothing open touches the V2 draft `moe_backend` path. The nearest related work is a cluster of V2 draft-config isolation fixes (#54731, #54716), which address different fields.

## Model evaluation

Not applicable. This changes which MoE kernel the *draft* is built with, and only when the user explicitly asks for one. With no `moe_backend` in the speculative config the behaviour is unchanged, which the second test pins. Affected configurations currently fail to start, so there is no baseline to regress against. Under real rejection sampling the target verifies every drafted token, so the draft's kernel choice cannot alter output.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used to author this change. I have reviewed every changed line, ran the tests and linters above myself, and can defend the design.

commits.pr_title: [Transformers] Generalize merged-column linear fusion
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Adds a generic `MergedColumnParallelFuser` to the Transformers backend's fuser system, as a structural fallback for column-parallel sibling projections that don't fit `GLUFuser`/`QKVFuser`'s specific patterns.

- **New fuser**: matches any set of ≥2 sibling linears fed the same placeholder input, rewrites `l1(x), l2(x), ... -> merged(x).split(sizes, -1)`, and merges them into one `MergedColumnParallelLinear`. Handles any number of projections with independent output sizes.
- **Collision-safe naming**: `merged_name` is a computed property, length-prefixed over the source projection names (`f"{len(name)}_{name}"` joined), so two different projection-name tuples can never produce the same attribute/`packed_modules_mapping` key. GLU/QKV/MLA keep their fixed conventional names (`gate_up_proj`, `qkv_proj`, `fused_qkv_a_proj`) since those always represent the same split.
- **Multi-candidate fusion selection**: `get_fusers` now caches every structurally-matching redefining fuser for a class, not just the first. `Fusers.__getitem__` then validates them per real instance and picks the first that passes, so a heterogeneous model (same Python class, differently-shaped layers) can fall back to the generic fuser on layers the specific one rejects, instead of silently missing fusion.
- **Dedup**: shared the merged-call-splice AST rewrite (`StackedFuser._splice_merged_split`) across `MergedColumnParallelFuser`, `QKVFuser`, and `MLAFuser`, removing three near-identical implementations.
- **Correctness fixes surfaced in review**: `GLUFuser.validate` now rejects mismatched gate/up `out_features` (an AndMul kernel requires an even split) instead of assuming `_get_glu_nodes`'s shared-input check made it redundant — fx's leaf-module tracing never validates shapes, so nothing else caught it.
- **Tests**: added coverage for arbitrary-arity merging, input-mutation rejection, `BroadcastGLU`/unfusable cases, `merged_name` uniqueness across different linear-name tuples, and the heterogeneous same-class fallback (`QKVFuser` vs `MergedColumnParallelFuser` chosen per-instance).

AI assistance was used.

## Test Plan

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/transformers/fusers`
- `VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/models/transformers/test_backend.py -k 'replace or vocab_tables or input_embeddings or tower_weights or marking'`
- `.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files tests/models/transformers/fusers/test_linear.py vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/__init__.py vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/base.py vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/glu.py vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/merged_column.py vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/mla.py vllm/model_executor/models/transformers/fusers/qkv.py`

## Test Results

- Related backend tests: 11 passed, 24 deselected.
- Pre-commit: all applicable hooks passed, including Ruff, formatting, mypy,

Build Python test dependencies in GNU C17 mode in both `vllm-test-deps` and `vllm-dev`. Keep the GCC 15/C++ toolchain and the vLLM production build flags unchanged, including AMX FP8 support. This is a functional image-build regression fix, not a warning suppression.

Duplicate checks: no open matching PR was found by searches for `pytrec`, `trec_eval`, `GCC C23`, or `49410 in:body`. No matching issue was found; unrelated search results were not used as issue links.

Validation:
- Local Linux aarch64 container, Ubuntu 25.10, GCC 15.2.0, uv-managed Python 3.12, package pinned to the exact CI version.

commits.pr_title: [Perf] Eliminate full-history reasoning scans for structured outputs
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose Structured-output constraints stay disabled until reasoning ends. Engine-based parsers currently find that boundary by reverse-scanning the full token history on every decode step—and at every draft position under speculative decoding. This makes the gate O(history) per check and O(n²) over a long reasoning generation. This PR derives safe, single-token reasoning-end IDs once per parser engine and scans only the new decode window. The existing monotonic `reasoning_ended` flag records the result, so no tracker or request lifecycle is added. Parsers without safely derivable IDs keep the legacy behavior. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["Decode or draft window"] --> B{"Safe engine end-token IDs?"} B -->|yes| C["Scan new tokens
O(delta)"] B -->|no| D["Legacy full-history scan
O(history)"] C --> E{"Reasoning end found?"} D --> E E -->|yes| F["Open structured-output gate"] E -->|no| G["Keep gate disabled"] ``` ## Test plan ### 1. Microbenchmark `StructuredOutputManager.should_advance` timed exactly as the scheduler calls it — once per request per engine step, with reasoning still in progress. Same script on both branches. | Parser | Reasoning tokens | `main` | this PR | |---|---|---|---| | qwen3 | 2,000 | 197.46 µs | **0.52 µs** | | qwen3 | 16,000 | 1486.89 µs | **0.52 µs** | | qwen3 | 64,000 | 6006.92 µs | **0.52 µs** | | deepseek_v4 (real tokenizer) | 2,000 | 94.79 µs | **0.55 µs** | | deepseek_v4 (real tokenizer) | 16,000 | 743.79 µs | **0.55 µs** | | deepseek_v4 (real tokenizer) | 64,000 | 2999.24 µs | **0.55 µs** | | deepseek_v32 (**fallback control**) | 2,000 | 18.07 µs | 16.30 µs | | deepseek_v32 (**fallback control**) | 16,000 | 125.93 µs | 125.82 µs | | deepseek_v32 (**fallback control**) | 64,000 | 507.33 µs | 499.87 µs | Cost is flat across a 32× range of history length, not merely lower. The `deepseek_v32` fallback control is unchanged within noise at every length, which is the evidence that the legacy branch is untouched rather than merely believed to be. ### 2. Live serving performance (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 8×H100) Streaming requests at concurrency 32, `chat_template_kwargs: {"thinking": true}`, so all four conditions for the gate to run are satisfied. Identical workload and server config within each pair; only the branch differs. commits.pr_title: [Core] Let SWA layers take the primary block size to avoid inflating the KV block LCM
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

An SWA layer started from the backend's smallest kernel block, so its
page divided a larger MLA page and unify scaled it by an integer ratio
to a block size coprime with the primary one (1024 B/token SWA draft
next to a 1152 B/token MLA target: 1728 vs 1536, scheduler LCM 13824),
which destroys prefix-cache granularity.

When the backend can run the primary block size unsplit (e.g. FlashAttn
via backend_per_kind.sliding_window), start from the primary block size

commits.pr_title: [Test] Dequantize NVFP4 KV cache scales in the layout the kernel writes
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`test_reshape_and_cache_flash[nvfp4]` fails on every Blackwell part with the current kernel, and nobody sees it because no CI job runs it on Blackwell.

`reshape_and_cache_flash` writes K block scales linearly and V block scales in the 4x4 swizzle of the SM100 trtllm-gen reader (`nvfp4_kv_cache_kernels.cu`, `kv == 0` branch vs `swizzle_scale_offset`). The test reference `dequant_nvfp4_kv_cache` unswizzles both, so the K comparison runs against a scrambled reference:

```
E  Mismatched elements: 989 / 10752 (9.2%)
E  Greatest absolute difference: nan at index (7, 6, 48) (up to 1.5 allowed)
```

The test is skipped below compute capability 10.0, and the `Kernels (B200)` job in `.buildkite/test_areas/kernels.yaml` does not run `kernels/attention` (the root misc job passes `--ignore=kernels/attention`), so the failure never reaches a CI run.

This PR fixes the test reference:

- `dequant_nvfp4_kv_cache` gets `swizzled_scales: bool = True`. Existing V callers are unchanged.
- K is dequantized linearly in `test_cache.py` (both nvfp4 tests) and in `test_flashinfer_trtllm_attention.py`.
- The V layout in `test_cache.py` follows the reader for the arch: swizzled on SM100, linear on SM12x (`current_platform.is_device_capability_family(120)`), which is what the FlashInfer paged reader on SM12x expects.

With that the test passes with the current kernel on SM100. On SM12x it fails on the V assert only, which is the writer behaviour tracked in #50084 and fixed in #46329. So this test turns #50084 from a code-reading argument into a red/green assertion.

Related: #50084, #46329, #54772.

## Test Plan

```bash
pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer_trtllm_attention.py tests/kernels/quantization/nvfp4_utils.py

pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k "nvfp4 and reshape_and_cache_flash" -v
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_cache.py -k 4over6 -v
```

I have no SM100 hardware. The SM100 path is unchanged in behaviour for V (still unswizzled) and only changes K from unswizzled to linear, which is what the kernel writes on every arch; a run on B200 would be appreciated.

## Test Result

RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell (sm_120), driver 580.173.02, vLLM v0.28.0 wheel, torch 2.13.0+cu130, `-k "nvfp4 and reshape_and_cache_flash and not unaligned and cuda and NHD and 64-8 and 1024"`:

| test files | writer | result |
|---|---|---|
| main, unchanged | stock kernel | 3 failed (K assert, 9-11 % mismatched, NaN) |
| main, unchanged | linear-V writer from #46329 | 3 failed (K assert) |
| this PR | stock kernel | 3 failed (V assert only, 9.5-10.9 % mismatched) |
| this PR | linear-V writer from #46329 | 3 passed |
| this PR, `-k 4over6` | stock kernel | 1 passed |

pre-commit: ruff check / ruff format / typos / mypy / SPDX all passed.

Byte-level check that motivated the change (one token written to slot 5, block 0, `head_size=64`, `block_size=16`): stock kernel leaves K scale row 5 populated and K scale rows 4, 6, 7 zero (linear), while V scale rows 4-7 all carry bytes (the 4-token swizzle group). The overlay writer leaves both K and V in row 5 only.
